title: The Golden State Killer Was Caught by His Cousins' DNA

narration: For decades, police had his DNA, but no name.
So they went looking for his cousins.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); scientist: examine -> hands_together -> worried -> point_up; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: For decades the killer's crime-scene DNA sat in evidence (collected in the 1970s-80s; DNA profiles later linked the crimes), but it matched no one in the FBI's national DNA database or California's databank, so investigators had no name. He had never been arrested for an offence that put his DNA on file.

Investigators searched a public genealogy database for the killer's relatives. DeAngelo had never submitted his own DNA to a genealogy database; the lead came from DNA profiles that distant relatives had uploaded and shared on GEDmatch.

narration: They called him the Golden State Killer.
He committed dozens of crimes from 1975 to 1986, including 13 murders.
shots.visual_description: gs10 suburb (night grade); gs10_man (silhouette): stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'THE GOLDEN STATE KILLER', card 'CALIFORNIA · 1975-1986 / DOZENS OF CRIMES / INCLUDING 13 MURDERS'.

overlays.text: CALIFORNIA · 1975-1986 / DOZENS OF CRIMES / INCLUDING 13 MURDERS

sources.claim_text: The crimes he admitted were committed in California between 1975 and 1986: dozens of crimes, including 13 murders (he pleaded guilty to 13 counts of first-degree murder and admitted dozens of uncharged crimes). Summary only; no detail used.

narration: Investigators uploaded his DNA to a free genealogy site: GEDmatch.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); examiner: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'UPLOADED: CRIME-SCENE DNA', label 'GEDMATCH'.

sources.claim_text: Investigators used crime-scene DNA to create a profile (reportedly under a pseudonym) on GEDmatch, a free public genealogy website where people upload and share DNA profiles to find relatives. GEDmatch said this was done without its knowledge.

narration: It didn't find the killer.
It found distant cousins.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit -> sit_slumped; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: GEDmatch returned distant relatives of the killer, reported as roughly third- to fourth-cousin matches.

narration: So they built family trees,
and narrowed them by age and location.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); examiner: stand -> point_up -> stand -> point_up; detective: arms_crossed -> read -> point_up -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: From those matches, investigators built family trees (reported as more than 25) and narrowed them to men of the right age who had lived in the right areas, which led to DeAngelo.

narration: The trees led to one man.
Joseph James DeAngelo.
shots.visual_description: gs10 driveway (warm grade); gs10_man (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense (walks); agent_a (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hand_to_face; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'THE TREES LED TO ONE MAN', card 'IDENTIFIED · APRIL 2018 / JOSEPH JAMES DEANGELO / 72 · CITRUS HEIGHTS, CALIFORNIA'.

sources.claim_text: From those matches, investigators built family trees (reported as more than 25) and narrowed them to men of the right age who had lived in the right areas, which led to DeAngelo.
The suspect identified was Joseph James DeAngelo, then 72, of Citrus Heights, a suburb of Sacramento.

narration: The twist? He was once a police officer.
He was fired in 1979, accused of shoplifting a hammer and dog repellent.
shots.visual_description: gs10 suburb (dawn grade); gs10_man (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hands_behind; gs10_man (silhouette): bowed -> stand (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: funfact 'He was still a police officer / when the crimes began. / (1973-1979)', stamp 'FIRED · 1979', label 'ACCUSED OF SHOPLIFTING'.

overlays.text: He was still a police officer / when the crimes began. / (1973-1979)

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: DeAngelo had been a police officer in two small California towns, Exeter and Auburn, between 1973 and 1979, so he was still an officer when the crimes began (1975).
He was fired from the Auburn police in 1979 after being accused of shoplifting a hammer and a can of dog repellent from a store.

narration: Now they needed his own DNA.
They followed him to a store, and swabbed his car's door handle.
shots.visual_description: gs10 store lot (warm grade); gs10_man (silhouette): stand (walks); agent_b: stand -> examine -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '18 APRIL 2018 · A STORE', callout 'HIS CAR'S DOOR HANDLE'.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC STORE

sources.claim_text: On 18 April 2018, according to the unsealed affidavit, detectives followed DeAngelo to a store in Roseville and swabbed the driver's-side door handle of his car while he shopped; the sample pointed to a match.

narration: Then they took a tissue from his trash.
The DNA was a conclusive match.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); scientist: stand -> examine -> hands_together -> realise; keyed camera moves; overlays: label '23 APRIL 2018 · HIS TRASH', label 'CONCLUSIVE MATCH', stamp 'MATCH'.

sources.claim_text: On 23 April 2018, investigators took a tissue from the trash outside his home; per the warrant, its DNA provided the conclusive match to the crime-scene profile.

narration: On April 24th, 2018, police arrested him outside his home.
shots.visual_description: gs10 driveway (warm grade); gs10_man (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hands_behind (walks); agent_a (silhouette): stand -> present (walks); agent_b (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> point (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '24 APRIL 2018 · CITRUS HEIGHTS'.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC HOUSE

sources.claim_text: DeAngelo was arrested outside his home in Citrus Heights (reported as in his driveway) on 24 April 2018. He was 72.

narration: In 2020, he pleaded guilty to 13 murders,
at a hearing held in a university ballroom.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (warm grade); judge (silhouette): sit -> sit_read -> sit; official (silhouette): hands_together -> read; gs10_man (silhouette): sit -> hands_together -> bowed; camera push/pull; overlays: card '29 JUNE 2020 · GUILTY PLEA / 13 MURDERS / 13 KIDNAPPINGS / + ADMITTED 161 UNCHARGED CRIMES', funfact 'The plea hearing was held / in a university ballroom, / for COVID distancing.'.

overlays.text: 29 JUNE 2020 · GUILTY PLEA / 13 MURDERS / 13 KIDNAPPINGS / + ADMITTED 161 UNCHARGED CRIMES

shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC ROOM

sources.claim_text: On 29 June 2020 he pleaded guilty to 13 counts of first-degree murder and 13 counts of kidnapping to commit robbery, and admitted 161 uncharged crimes, which could no longer be charged because of the statute of limitations. The deal took the death penalty off the table.
FUN FACT: the plea hearing was held in a ballroom at Sacramento State university, used as a makeshift courtroom to allow social distancing during COVID-19.

narration: His sentence: life without parole, eleven times over.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); judge (silhouette): sit -> gavel -> sit -> sit_read; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'SENTENCED · 21 AUGUST 2020 / 11 CONSECUTIVE LIFE TERMS / WITHOUT PAROLE / PLUS FURTHER TERMS'.

overlays.text: SENTENCED · 21 AUGUST 2020 / 11 CONSECUTIVE LIFE TERMS / WITHOUT PAROLE / PLUS FURTHER TERMS

sources.claim_text: On 21 August 2020, Judge Michael Bowman sentenced him to 11 consecutive life terms without the possibility of parole, plus further terms (reported by AP as 15 life terms with the possibility of parole and eight years).

narration: Decades without a name, ended by a family tree and a tissue in the trash.
Next: the Great Train Robbery, and a Monopoly board.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); scientist: hands_together -> examine -> point -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: nextcase '£2.6 million. A mail train. / And a Monopoly board.'.

sources.claim_text: From those matches, investigators built family trees (reported as more than 25) and narrowed them to men of the right age who had lived in the right areas, which led to DeAngelo.
On 23 April 2018, investigators took a tissue from the trash outside his home; per the warrant, its DNA provided the conclusive match to the crime-scene profile.

Next-case tease: in the Great Train Robbery (8 August 1963) a gang stole about 2.6 million pounds from a Royal Mail train; fingerprints on a Monopoly board at their farm hideout helped lead police to them. (Narration names only the robbery and 'a Monopoly board'; the card shows the amount.)
